item.title: Bridging digitalisation, sustainability, and resilience through systems thinking tools: Integrated perspectives and collaborative practices for SMEs
item.content:encoded:
Rui Torres de Oliveira, Deakin University

Agnes Toth-Peter, University of Queensland

Martie-Louise Verreynne, University of Queensland

David Audretsch, Indiana University

Domenico Dentoni, MBS School of Business

Andrea Chiarini, University of Verona

The 21st century presents a range of complex and interdependent challenges, including climate change, resource depletion, economic inequality, and technological disruptions. These so-called wicked problems demand a paradigm shift in our approach to problem-solving. Addressing such challenges requires multi-stakeholder partnerships and holistic, systems-level approaches that transcend traditional, siloed methodologies. Systems thinking, a powerful tool for understanding complexity and interconnections, offers a pathway to sustainable solutions.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Applications of systems thinking tools, such as causal loop diagrams (CLDs), system archetypes, and system dynamics modeling, in addressing sustainability challenges
  • Development and validation of systems-level frameworks and methodologies for sustainable development
  • Case studies demonstrating the impact of systems thinking on real-world sustainability and/or digitalisation initiatives
  • Use of group model building and participatory system dynamics to support interdisciplinary and ecosystem solutions
  • Exploration of system archetypes and system dynamics models to identify leverage points for driving transformational change and to investigate levers in cross-boundary settings
  • The role of digital technologies, including IoT, AI, big data, and blockchain, in enabling systems-level insights and solutions in the circular economy and sustainability initiatives
  • Integration of digitalisation with circular economy strategies and Industry 5.0 principles and potentials
  • Innovative approaches to digital transformation that promote sustainable development
  • Cross-sectoral and interdisciplinary research to foster collaboration in bridging sustainability and digitalisation, using systems thinking
  • The role of ecosystems in sustainable business models and the boundaries of entrepreneurial ecosystems
  • Methodologies for recognising, assessing and addressing the interconnectedness of environmental, economic, and social systems
  • Open innovation in new sustainable businesses, considering distinct institutional contexts and economic systems, such as emerging and developed economies
